data.hypothesis: A two-group scalar schedule that interleaves independent table lookups may overlap lookup latency while amortizing loop control. Committing the first block only after its own validity check preserves fallback position if the second block is invalid. Prior unroll factors were slower than baseline, so this tests a scheduling variant, not an assumed speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Inform future scalar-unroll trials; correctness cause for the failed two-group variant is not established.
memory_lessons.claim: The four-group candidate was the fastest measured T3 unroll (63.81 µs), but still slower than the 55.00 µs baseline; three- and eight-group candidates were slower still at 147.64 µs and 81.30 µs. A two-group candidate also failed a protected case, so this proposal retains conservative two-block safety and fallback handling.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Have the controller test correctness on short inputs, block boundaries, padding and Lena, then compare repeated native timings; retain no speedup claim absent those measurements.

data.notes: No commands were run and no validation or timing is claimed here. The controller should evaluate empty/short inputs, group boundaries, padding cases, random valid inputs and Lena before timing. Previously measured unroll means were 82.32 µs (2 groups), 147.64 µs (3), 63.81 µs (4) and 81.30 µs (8), all slower than the 55.00 µs baseline; one distinct two-group variant failed a protected Lena case. This version uses a 21-character guard so each of the two blocks meets the original single-block loop's 13-character safety condition in turn.
transformations: Unrolled the safe decode loop by two eight-character blocks when at least 21 input characters remain.
Interleaved scalar table lookups for independent blocks, then validated and stored the first block before committing the second.
If the first block is invalid, fall through to the existing scalar decoder without advancing; if only the second is invalid, keep the first block's output and resume at the second block.
Preserved the existing scalar tail, padding, and invalid-input path; added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-size specialization, or thread-budget changes.
